paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: in this passage, the gallows Haman built for Mordecai is the one he ends up on. Scripture says it plainly: "So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai." (Esther 7:10) I'm not saying every scheme in the world turns around like this, but here it did, and the king's fury subsided. Haman put all that effort into a plan against somebody else, and that same plan is what met him.

Now look at Esther, because she matters just as much. She was the one who had to open her mouth and say, "grant me my life as my petition, and the lives of my people as my request." (Esther 7:3) I think that took everything she had. Her words are what got the king asking, "Who is this, and where is the one who would devise such a scheme?" (Esther 7:5), and when the moment finally came, she spoke.

So what does this mean for you, baker? When you know the right thing to say and your moment finally shows up, speak, even if your voice shakes a little. Esther didn't get to see the whole road ahead of her, and neither do we. And hold on tight, friend, because this story is NOT done.
